Claire — thanks again for the overview. Below is a condensed post-call recap + recommended next steps we propose for a 3-week eval. I kept the exec notes first for procurement, followed by model recommendations and the bench artifacts we recorded during a representative run.

Executive summary (for procurement)
- Goal: Validate generation quality for clinical note summarization while meeting latency SLOs and predictable cost per 1k tokens.
- Recommended approach: 3-week pilot: 1) hosted sandbox (Redwood hosted) for rapid functional eval; 2) dedicated GPU pool (on-prem or VPC) for performance verification at scale; 3) optional private deployment for PHI tests.
- Estimated delta vs current: ~20-35% lower per-token cost with KV-caching + q4_0 quantization profiles while holding p95 latency within 2x of baseline model.

Model recommendations (prioritized for fit & ops):
1) Redwood-13B-v2 (FP16 / q4_0 profile) — best latency/quality tradeoff; strong on structured clinical prompts and cheap to run for high TPS.
   - Verified perf (single RTX A5000-like node): p50 18ms, p95 82ms, p99 190ms, sustained parse-rate 240 TPS on 512-token avg seq (batching tuned).
2) Llama-2-13B-chat (int8 / optimized kernels) — slightly better instruction-following on rare clinical phrasing; p50 25ms, p95 105ms, p99 230ms, sustained 190 TPS.
3) Llama-2-70B (sharded) — highest quality for edge cases; expect materially higher cost and 3-4x latency; suggested only for edge fallback.

Quality/regression guardrails
- We'll provide a prompt suite (attached prompt-set-v1.txt) and a small regression set (200 clinical pairs) to monitor ROUGE and hallucination metrics.
- Recommended automatic fallback: If p95 latency > 180ms, route to a smaller validated variant with an expanded prompt/context compression step.

Artifacts & links (benchmarks recorded on Nov 10, representative workload)
- Synapse Benchmark Summary: synapse_benchmark_summary.pdf (attached) — includes end-to-end traces, p50/p95/p99, and cost breakdown.
- Runtime trace (raw): runtime-trace-20261110.json (attached) — shows batching distribution and KV cache hit-rates ~28%.
- Prompt set: prompt-set-v1.txt (attached) — 32 prompts used for qualitative checks.
- Live proof: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/Synapse-Eval-Pack-20261110

Proposed timeline (3 weeks)
Week 1 — hosted sandbox (functional quality & integration)
Week 2 — dedicated capacity tests (throughput, sustained TPS, latency p99 checks)
Week 3 — security review and procurement packet; finalize rollout policy and SLA requirements.

Next steps / asks
- Claire: confirm access window for sample PHI data or sanitized substitute; procurement point-of-contact so we can prepare the cost sheet.
- Ben: Ben will share the bench packet and a short runbook for the dedicated test.
- Soojin: please review the runtime traces and add any ops-level observations (limits, burst handling, KV cache tuning).

Thanks — I'll follow up with a one-page procurement summary and the HubSpot deal record.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai

Subject: Bench artifacts + concise perf table (Synapse sample workload)

Claire / Lauren — attaching the benchmark summary and raw trace from our representative run. Key datapoints below (all measured on an A5000-equivalent instance with Redwood runtime defaults and KV caching enabled):

Perf table (representative config)
- Redwood-13B-v2 (FP16 / q4_0): p50 18ms | p95 82ms | p99 190ms | sustained 240 TPS (512-token avg, batching target 128)
- Llama-2-13B-chat (int8): p50 25ms | p95 105ms | p99 230ms | sustained 190 TPS
- Llama-2-70B (sharded, 2-node): p50 120ms | p95 480ms | p99 980ms | sustained 45 TPS

Ops notes (Soojin + infra)
- KV cache hit-rate for this workload was 28% — enabling prefix caching for repeated patient templates should push this above 45% and materially reduce per-token spend.
- Batching knob: we recommend starting with batching target 64 for the hosted sandbox; ramp to 128 in dedicated to saturate GPU without hurting p99.
- Quantization: q4_0 gave the best latency/quality balance in our A/B; we can run a quick A/B on a subset of your regression prompts if you want explicit delta numbers.

Attachments:
- synapse_benchmark_summary.pdf (PDF, 920KB)
- runtime-trace-20261110.json (JSON, 2.3MB)
- prompt-set-v1.txt (TEXT, 4KB)

I'll add these to the Drive link for the deal as well. Claire — if you can share a procurement contact, we'll produce a concise 1-page cost + compliance summary (SLA, data handling modes, KMS options).

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineering — Redwood Inference

Claire — quick ops confirmation from my side: the traces show a transient p99 spike at 21:34 on Nov 10 correlated with an unanticipated long prompt (2.4k tokens). Actionable notes:
- Add a presubmission compressor for lengthy notes (we can provide a light transform that clips context and appends a deterministic summary).
- For the dedicated run, reserve a small burst buffer (2x baseline capacity) to absorb ingestion spikes for 2–3 minutes.
- We'll instrument a p95 SLA guardrail and an automated fallback route to Redwood-13B-v2-small if p95 > 180ms for two consecutive 5-minute windows.

I'll schedule a 30-minute runbook walkthrough (propose Nov 16 at 10:00 AM PT). If that works, Ben and I will bring the bench slides and a short demo of the fallback routing.

— Soojin
